title: Shared-classifier attention and mean pooling control
hypothesis: Replacing the selected parent's ordinary log-mean-exp (LME) branch with a uniform mean of the same instance logits may improve worst-view development AUROC by removing the direct branch's positive-tail emphasis while retaining the learned attention branch. The parent passed the search score gate, yet its paired logit margin decreased in all six seed/noise conditions and negative-bag probability increased in all six. This motivates a matched negative control for the LME-specific explanation. Both models use the same encoder, gated attention, shared classifier, parameter count and fixed equal blend. A mean-control gain with better paired discrimination and margin retention would be consistent with reduced sensitivity to high background scores. A loss would be consistent with useful tail evidence or greater dilution under uniform averaging. Neither outcome identifies patch-level tumor evidence or isolates pooling from changed optimization.
note: Public summary; full source quotations and agent logs are not redistributed.
